arcs.title: Middle East Supply Shock: The Crude Surge
arcs.summary: Iran-Israel tensions pushed WTI from $89 to $96.41 as the market priced in a Hormuz supply premium. MCX crude crossed ₹9,000 for the first time this year — HPCL and IndiGo are repricing exposure in real time.
arcs.outcome: MCX Crude retreated from the ₹9,000 key level back to ₹7,615 as the geopolitical supply premium from Iran-Israel tensions dissipated and market participants unwound their bullish exposure.

arcs.title: Iran-US Peace Talks Collapse: Safe-Haven Gold Rebounds
arcs.summary: Iran publicly rejects key US peace conditions, reversing diplomatic optimism and triggering a flight-to-safety rally in gold while crude remains under pressure.

arcs.title: Iran-US Peace Deal: Fear Premium Unwind
arcs.summary: Iran-US peace negotiations continue at reduced tempo while Middle East tensions re-escalate, reversing crude's fear-premium unwind as WTI rebounds to $70.02/bbl while gold remains under pressure.
arcs.outcome: Arc went 5 days without a new edition — narrative faded

arcs.title: US Summer Cooling Demand Drives Natural Gas Spike
arcs.summary: Henry Hub natural gas futures surged 4.31% overnight on above-normal summer cooling demand forecasts across the US South and revised LNG export terminal throughput estimates, with spillover impact on MCX NatGas (+3.80%).
arcs.outcome: The natural gas spike faded without reaching the ₹314.5/mmBtu key level, leaving MCX NatGas at ₹304 as the cooling demand narrative lost traction after five days.

arcs.title: Crude's Geopolitical Premium: A Three-Day Spike and Fade
arcs.summary: Renewed Middle East tensions pushed WTI crude from $72.35 to $74.15 over two sessions, with MCX Crude jumping from ₹6885 to ₹7073 as the market priced in a fresh supply-risk premium. By day three the premium began fading — WTI eased back to $72.29 and MCX Crude retreated to ₹6913 — even as copper signaled a broader industrial recovery, fracturing the unified fear-trade narrative.

arcs.title: Precious Metals Unwind as FOMC Hawkish Stance & Middle East Easing Reduce Safe-Haven Demand
arcs.summary: Gold and silver rally sharply as weaker US non-farm payrolls data trigger FOMC rate-cut reassessment, reversing the safe-haven unwind and reducing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding precious metals.
